name: Andhra Pradesh
note: CLM chapter 32 records Telugu and Urdu. English continues for specified purposes. https://web.archive.org/web/20171011124847id_/http://nclm.nic.in/shared/linkimages/NCLM52ndReport.pdf#page=120

name: Arunachal Pradesh
note: The administration reported English. The English name serves as the display name.

name: Assam
note: Bodo is an associate official language. Bengali applies in the Barak Valley. English continues for specified purposes.

name: Bihar
note: CLM chapter 9 records Urdu as an additional official language. https://web.archive.org/web/20171011124847id_/http://nclm.nic.in/shared/linkimages/NCLM52ndReport.pdf#page=41

name: Chhattisgarh
note: Chhattisgarhi has official status. The state portal uses Hindi for its title.

name: Goa
note: The 1987 Act names Konkani as the official language and permits Marathi for official purposes. Section 4 provides for continued use of English. https://www.goa.gov.in/department/official-language/

name: Gujarat
note: Section 2 of the Gujarat Official Languages Act authorises Gujarati and Hindi. The district portal uses Gujarati for the state name.

name: Haryana
note: Punjabi is the second language under the 2010 amendment. The CLM records the continued use of English. https://web.archive.org/web/20171011124847id_/http://nclm.nic.in/shared/linkimages/NCLM52ndReport.pdf#page=29

name: Himachal Pradesh
note: The 2019 amendment adds Sanskrit as the second official language.

name: Jharkhand
note: Hindi is the first official language. The CLM report predates later language additions. The current list needs a check against the consolidated state Act.

name: Karnataka
note: The district portal uses Kannada for state branding. CLM chapter 29 records Kannada. https://web.archive.org/web/20171011124847id_/http://nclm.nic.in/shared/linkimages/NCLM52ndReport.pdf#page=104

name: Kerala
note: The state portal writes the Malayalam name as shown. English may also be used for official purposes.

name: Madhya Pradesh
note: The district portal uses Hindi for state branding. CLM chapter 12 records Hindi. https://web.archive.org/web/20171011124847id_/http://nclm.nic.in/shared/linkimages/NCLM52ndReport.pdf#page=50

name: Maharashtra
note: CLM chapter 30 records Marathi. https://web.archive.org/web/20171011124847id_/http://nclm.nic.in/shared/linkimages/NCLM52ndReport.pdf#page=113

name: Manipur
note: The 2021 amendment defines Manipuri as Meeteilon in Meetei Mayek and allows concurrent Bengali script for up to ten years from 10 Mar 2021. The state language directorate uses the displayed spelling on page 10 of its Manipuri course reader. https://web.archive.org/web/20240921020413id_/https://dlpi.mn.gov.in/media/filer_public/6c/c4/6cc49b48-7b45-4415-a866-9f64297a7e5c/bcom1stsem___mil.pdf#page=10

name: Meghalaya
note: The 2026 ordinance names English, Khasi and Garo. I could not locate its commencement notice or a replacement Act. The display name uses Latin script. https://newsonair.gov.in/meghalaya-declares-khasi-and-garo-as-official-languages-alongside-english/

name: Mizoram
note: The 1974 state Act names Mizo and allows continued use of English. The CLM report also lists Hindi. Mizo uses Latin script.

name: Nagaland
note: The English name serves as the display name.

name: Odisha
note: The Chief Minister portal uses Odia. Unicode calls the script Oriya. https://web.archive.org/web/20171011124847id_/http://nclm.nic.in/shared/linkimages/NCLM52ndReport.pdf#page=80

name: Punjab
note: CLM chapter 7 specifies Gurmukhi. https://web.archive.org/web/20171011124847id_/http://nclm.nic.in/shared/linkimages/NCLM52ndReport.pdf#page=37

name: Rajasthan
note: The CLM records Hindi and the additional use of English.

name: Sikkim
note: The 1977 Act names Nepali, Bhutia and Lepcha and allows continued use of English. The list includes later additions. The consolidated amendments need a check. https://web.archive.org/web/20180722164022id_/https://www.sikkim.gov.in/stateportal/UsefulLinks/Gazette1977.pdf

name: Tamil Nadu
note: English continues for communication. CLM chapter 36 records Tamil and that use of English. https://web.archive.org/web/20171011124847id_/http://nclm.nic.in/shared/linkimages/NCLM52ndReport.pdf#page=137

name: Telangana
note: The 2017 amendment made Urdu the second official language across the state. The state portal uses Telugu in its press releases.

name: Tripura
note: CLM section 23.2 lists all three languages. The Khowai district portal uses the Bengali state name. https://web.archive.org/web/20171011124847id_/http://nclm.nic.in/shared/linkimages/NCLM52ndReport.pdf#page=84

name: Uttar Pradesh
note: The 1989 amendment provides for Urdu as a second official language for specified purposes. https://web.archive.org/web/20171011124847id_/http://nclm.nic.in/shared/linkimages/NCLM52ndReport.pdf#page=54

name: Uttarakhand
note: The 2010 state Act gives Sanskrit second official language status.

name: West Bengal
note: The district site uses Bengali for state branding. Several additional languages apply only in specified areas. The consolidated amendments need a check.

name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
note: CLM section 31.3 records Hindi and English. The district portal uses this Hindi form for the territory. https://web.archive.org/web/20171011124847id_/http://nclm.nic.in/shared/linkimages/NCLM52ndReport.pdf#page=115

name: Chandigarh
note: CLM section 2.3 names English. The English name serves as the display name.

name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

name: Delhi
note: Punjabi and Urdu have second official language status. English continues for official purposes. https://web.archive.org/web/20171011124847id_/http://nclm.nic.in/shared/linkimages/NCLM52ndReport.pdf#page=18

name: Jammu and Kashmir
note: The UT name appears in Urdu in the government branding on the Srinagar district portal. Section 3 of the 2020 Act lists all five languages. https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2020/222037.pdf

name: Ladakh
note: The UT masthead uses this Hindi form. Section 3 of the 2025 regulation names all five languages and provides for a start date by notice. https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2025/263538.pdf

name: Lakshadweep
note: CLM section 34.2 names English. Malayalam is widely spoken. The English name serves as the display name.

name: Puducherry
note: The 1965 Act names Tamil, allows Malayalam for Mahe and Telugu for Yanam, and permits English for official purposes. https://web.archive.org/web/20240315060504id_/https://law.py.gov.in/docs/Code1.pdf
